speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: To encourage the use of intellectual property (IP) arising from taxpayer’s research and development (R&D) activities, the Minister for Finance had announced in Budget 2017 that an IP Development Incentive (IDI) will be introduced.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Clauses 2, 5 and 9 amend sections 3 and 19M, and introduce section 19A to give legislative effect to this change.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The second change is to enhance the Integrated Investment Allowance (IIA).

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The IIA scheme provides additional allowance to a taxpayer who has incurred fixed capital expenditure on qualifying equipment used abroad by an overseas company for approved projects.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Currently, to qualify for the allowance, the overseas company is required to use the qualifying equipment wholly for the approved projects.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Clauses 10 to 13 give legislative effect to this change.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The remaining legislative changes arising from our periodic review of the income tax system are either administrative or technical in nature.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: These changes also reflect the Government’s commitment to keep Singapore competitive and relevant as a place for investment as our external economic conditions change.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, I support the amendment of the Economic Expansion Incentives Bill.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Timely changes in tax incentives would enable Singapore to maintain its global competitiveness and attract even more multinational companies (MNCs) into Singapore to contribute to our national economy.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Today, I would like to share my views regarding the proposed amendments from two perspectives – that of the business community, as well as of taxpayers.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: MNCs and local enterprises are the two large engines which steer Singapore’s economic development.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: MNCs which come to Singapore, besides directly creating employment opportunities, also spur the development of related industries.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Some local companies have leveraged the opportunities of collaborating with MNCs to improve the technology content of their products and services and have gradually become world-class companies.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: This win-win collaborative model is the outcome businesses look forward to most.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: After going through the Bill, I would like to focus on one new content in particular: the new section 97ZHA states that after companies have successfully applied for the IIA, in the event that they fail to comply with any term or condition as specified, or the outcome indicators, not only will the tax incentive be terminated, the Government can also recover this particular investment allowance already given.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Recently, the Government has mentioned many times that Government expenditure would steadily increase, and that we need to explore new sources of income and curb expenditure.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: One of the ways is to strengthen the supervision of tax incentives and guard against abuse.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The amended Bill would enable stronger auditing and oversight of the tax incentives.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Also, I would like to ask the Minister if the current amendment to the Bill was spurred by an increase in the number of errant cases in recent years.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Of greater concern to businesses is that the value-add effect on local companies brought about by such tax incentives to attract foreign investment seems to have waned.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Quite a number of businesses have told me that they miss the Local Industry Upgrading Programme (LIUP) which was phased out in 2010.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The programme, extremely useful then in promoting win-win collaboration between foreign investors and local enterprises, continues to be well-regarded today.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: In the earlier years, foreign companies which invested in the traditional sectors here could generate significant opportunities and value-add for related or supporting local companies both downstream and upstream and create direct and indirect employment opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: However, in recent years, most of the MNCs attracted to Singapore are in the emerging sectors which establish their regional headquarters or R&D centres here.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The activities which can create value-add for local companies, such as product design, manufacturing, industry supply chain and distribution are, however, located in other countries in the region.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: It is no longer easy for local enterprises to take the local advantage in becoming service providers for the MNCs like before.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, our small and medium enterprises (SMEs) should step up venturing overseas, in line with the Government policy to encourage businesses to internationalise.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: They can then continue to service the MNCs which have established production bases in the region.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: I also urge the Government agencies under the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI), namely, the Economic Development Board (EDB) and Enterprise Singapore (ESG), to continue to work closely with local industries.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: We hope that EDB, whilst continuing to attract high quality foreign investors into Singapore, would also make capability upgrading of local enterprises a key objective – to provide MNCs and local enterprises with a win-win collaborative model to become the driving force of Singapore’s future economic development.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is encouraging that the Government continues to support companies through tax reliefs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, I would like to seek some clarifications and offer some suggestions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: First, clause 2 of the Bill amends section 3 of the Act by inserting a new definition of "Intellectual Property Income".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is defined as "any intellectual property income prescribed by the Minister under section 102".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Section 102 of the Act, amongst other things, empowers the Minister to make regulations that may be necessary or expedient for purposes of carrying out provisions of the Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: What are the assessment criteria that will be considered by the Minister in prescribing a particular income as IP Income?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will this be based on quantitative or qualitative data?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The reason I am asking is because greater transparency and less ambiguity in the legislation itself will only enable Pioneer Service Companies and Development and Expansion Companies to better understand what constitutes IP Income and, correspondingly, whether their activities will fall under the tax incentive scheme.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that EDB does publish guidelines from time to time on its website, such as guidelines related to the Pioneer Certificate Incentive (PC) and DEI.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, if the principle behind the Act and this Bill is to encourage companies to grow capabilities, develop high-value and substantive economic activities, through tax reliefs, then it is crucial for companies to have a clear understanding of what the parameters are for them to qualify for tax reliefs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A clear understanding will allow companies to better plan their business and growth strategies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I raised a related point in 2016 during the previous iteration of the Economic Expansion Incentives (Relief from Income Tax) (Amendment) Bill on the need to have clearer qualifying criteria for PC and DEI.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Then, Minister Lim Hng Kiang replied that it is a balance between clarity, transparency and ensuring we remain flexible and responsive to the increasingly complex economic environment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand the Minister's point, but I have two follow-up queries.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One, I think responsiveness can be achieved through the mechanism of legislative amendments, which allows the Government to continually review the incentives and schemes to maintain their relevance.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This possibly explains why we are legislating amendments to the Act via this Bill within a relatively short period of time from the last amendment in March 2016.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Two, flexibility may also be achieved through the actual operative provisions in the Bill, instead of relying on broad definitions of a key term.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I note that the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) published a table stating that IDI incorporates the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development's (OECD's) Base Erosion and Profit Shifting reports (BEPS)-compliant modified nexus approach and it is meant to encourage the exploitation of IP arising from R&D activities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify how the IDI works in practice with the legislative amendments in this Bill?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On the point of BEPS, I understand from a Facebook feedback by Mr Gregg Fong that as a result of the BEPS framework, tax authorities globally have put in place more stringent rules to ensure taxpayers pay their fair share of taxes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Therefore, it is unwise to assume that tax incentives remain attractive for MNCs in this post-BEPS era, and now, more so than ever, tax incentives need to make business sense for MNCs and economic sense for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this context, the queries raised by Mr Fong are: how do these Bill amendments and the existing broader tax incentive schemes fit in with Singapore's broader strategic goals?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Fong pointed out that, historically, the initial intention of tax incentives was to attract top MNCs to invest in Singapore, and this worked very well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The tax incentives were then gradually tweaked as Singapore’s economy grew.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister explain how the current amendments adjust the tax incentives such that they remain relevant and are aligned with Singapore's current strategic goals?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And can the Minister clarify what these amendments will mean for companies which did invest and are continually investing in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Also, do the existing tax incentive schemes and these amendments ensure fair employment opportunities for Singaporeans in managerial positions?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Fong clarified that this query is not coming from a place of an anti-foreigner sentiment, but it is taking a practical approach as, logically, MNCs would enjoy significant costs savings, from such tax incentive schemes and general manpower costs savings, if they are able to upskill Singaporeans over a period of time and transfer these skills from expatriate foreigners to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Third, on a broader practical level, how do these legislative amendments and various schemes and incentives from Government agencies, such as EDB and the Standards, Productivity and Innovation Board (SPRING) Singapore, all work together from the perspective of an SME which wishes to take advantage of these available tools?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Hence, it is natural that bigger companies qualify.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Smaller companies are able to respond and react to market conditions and remain agile and flexible.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Thus, it appears that SMEs, by their very nature, are better placed to embrace innovation and position their businesses to adapt to changes rapidly, in line with the principles of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The Economic Expansion Incentives Act, which was introduced by the Government in recent years, was meant to encourage companies to continue introducing high value-added activities in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The overarching objective of such incentive schemes was not just to serve as an encouragement to the targeted industries and companies, but also to encourage companies to stay relevant in this fast-changing knowledge-based and technology-driven economy and being able to provide economic value to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The technologies developed should be able to make them more competitive and simultaneously create new higher value-added skilled jobs for our local workforce.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: This will, in turn, enable the workforce to move upstream, thereby creating higher value at work and increase productivity.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: This symbiotic relationship between the industry and the Government is highly commendable.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: The proposed six amendments to the Economic Expansion Act are reasonable in my opinion.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: However, I believe it is apt as Singapore's economic landscape has moved from a labour-intensive to a knowledge-intensive one, with a high skills-based platform.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Thus, after many years of investing and working with the industry, it is reasonable to expect that IP should be one of the main activities of the affected companies.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Thus, it is also reasonable to consider income from IP as a source of revenue in the current context in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I believe there are pockets of local SMEs which are stuck in their business activities in the old and traditional way.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: While they may not be seen as high-tech, but they do serve the need of the larger Singapore labour workforce by providing jobs.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Thus, I would like to suggest that the incentive as previously prescribed should be extended to the smaller SMEs and perhaps, more should be done to assist them to move up the ladder in implementing technology in their business activities.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: As an example, I would like to highlight the cleaning industry and the small public works contractor industry.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Smaller SMEs are hardest hit with the constant disruption which is prevailing at smaller intervals, from financial technology (fintech) to augment the reality.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Smaller SMEs find it harder to cope as they do not have the muscle and capacity to spend in R&D work, less IP work.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: And when they do, it will be a strain on their business operations.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, the extension of the prevailing scheme to smaller SMEs will go a long way.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: I plead with the Government to consider and review this.

speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
text: With that, Mr Speaker, notwithstanding the suggestion I made, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: As all three of them mentioned, these amendments are very important, and we have to see how these amendments fit in with our overall strategic goal for Singapore, which is to encourage companies to continue to undertake investment, expand their capabilities and create new jobs.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: To do so, our economic agencies require a suite of tools to engage our companies and, therefore, our Government regularly reviews our incentives and schemes, be it tax incentives or non-tax incentives, to ensure that they continue to be relevant and effective as our economic and operating environment continues to evolve.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Companies that are committed to undertake substantive economic investments and create good job opportunities in Singapore can continue to benefit from the PSC and DEI schemes.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Meanwhile, we will continue to encourage the use of IPs arising from a taxpayer’s R&D activities under the new IDI.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Taxpayers can apply for IDI regardless of whether they are currently on PSC and DEI or not.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: In this regard, the Government has proactively reached out to the companies and consulted them on the draft legislation.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: This, among other things, includes the definition of IP Income, which will be made clear in the subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: As I mentioned in the earlier debate in 2016, it is better and more effective for us to define IP Income in the subsidiary legislation than in the main legislation so that the objective is still achieved.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: You have transparency, clarity and, at the same time, you have more responsiveness and flexibility by doing so in subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: So, these amendments in this Bill will help to provide our companies that have invested in or are continuing to invest in Singapore with more certainty.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: This is because our incentives have been reviewed by the international community and they meet international tax standards ahead of many other countries and jurisdictions, which are still in the midst of reviewing their tax regimes.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: We remain committed to being a competitive location for anchoring substantive economic activities and will continue to monitor global developments.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: On Mr Louis Ng’s point about fair employment practices, we support that and we agree that companies recognise the commercial value of having such practices in place.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: This is because by hiring fairly and based on merit, companies would have access to a wider talent pool and reap the benefits from increased productivity.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: The Singapore Government, of course, helps our companies to develop the career of Singaporeans in their employment.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: In our engagements with companies, we work with them to develop training and career development programmes for their employees, for example, the SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative (LDI) is one such schemes that employers registered or incorporated in Singapore can leverage to create and enhance in-house leadership development programmes.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: These programmes, which are company-centric and sector-specific, can also be implemented through collaborations with external training providers.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Mr Thomas Chua has accurately pointed out the value of having both MNCs and local enterprises in our ecosystem to drive our economic growth.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Azmoon Ahmad have asked how SMEs can benefit from these amendments.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: In general, our tax incentives, including the ones in EEIA, are open to application by all companies, regardless of size, as long as they are able to commit to making significant contributions to our economy.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: In this instance, with the liberalisation of IIA, SMEs can enjoy more flexibility in their business arrangements with their foreign counterparts.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: I would also like to clarify one of the points that Mr Thomas Chua mentioned regarding LIUP.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: The second point that Mr Thomas Chua mentioned about the new section 97ZHA, it has always been our practice that if the companies do not adequately meet up to their commitments set out in the incentives, we will withdraw the incentives and recover the incentives made to them.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: This section is just to regularise our practice.

speaker: Mr Lim Hng Kiang
text: The Government will continue to recover the IIA awarded if the company fails any conditions or breaches the legislative amendments.
